21.note: Cleartext credential/file transfer protocol; prefer SFTP/FTPS.

22.note: Exposed remote administration; ensure key-based auth and rate limiting.

23.note: Unencrypted remote administration protocol; should not be internet-facing.

25.note: Mail relay exposure; check for open relay / spoofing protections.

53.note: DNS service exposed; check for zone transfer (AXFR) misconfiguration.

80.note: Expected web service port; verify it redirects to HTTPS.

111.note: RPC portmapper; historically used in enumeration and DoS chains.

135.note: Windows RPC endpoint mapper; common lateral-movement target.

139.note: Legacy Windows file-sharing protocol; frequent target for enumeration.

445.note: SMB exposed to the network; high-value target for worms and lateral movement (e.g. EternalBlue).

1433.note: Database service should not be directly internet-facing.

1521.note: Database service should not be directly internet-facing.

3306.note: Database service should not be directly internet-facing.

3389.note: Remote Desktop exposed to the internet is a top ransomware initial-access vector.

5432.note: Database service should not be directly internet-facing.

5900.note: VNC often has weak/no authentication by default.

6379.note: Redis has no authentication by default in many deployments and is routinely mass-scanned.

8080.note: Alternate HTTP port; check whether it is an unintended admin/dev interface.

8443.note: Alternate HTTPS port; check whether it is an unintended admin/dev interface.

9200.note: Elasticsearch is frequently exposed without authentication, leaking indexed data.

27017.note: MongoDB has historically shipped with no authentication by default and is a top data-exposure source.
